facts.statement: Pachycostasaurus is an extinct genus of marine reptile.
facts.quote: genus: Pachycostasaurus

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is Pachycostasaurus dawni.
facts.quote: species: dawni

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was discovered by amateur geologist Alan Dawn in a quarry in Peterborough.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil of Pachycostasaurus was discovered by Alan Dawn, an amateur geologist and museum volunteer, in what is now a quarry in Peterborough.

facts.statement: The fossil was formally described in 1996 by Arthur Cruickshank, David Martill, and Leslie Noè.
facts.quote: The fossil was described in 1996 by Palaeontologists Arthur Cruickshank, David Martill and Leslie Noè

facts.statement: Pachycostasaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Jurassic

facts.statement: Fossils of Pachycostasaurus have been found in the Oxford Clay formation of Peterborough, England.
facts.quote: Pachycostasaurus (meaning 'thick-ribbed lizard') is an extinct Pliosauroid from the Oxford Clay formation of Peterborough, England.

facts.statement: The single known specimen of Pachycostasaurus dawni is approximately 3 meters long.
facts.quote: The type species, P. dawni, is represented by a single near complete specimen (PETMG R338) which was approximately 3 m long.

facts.statement: Pachycostasaurus is defined by its large, sausage-like ribs and gastralia.
facts.quote: Perhaps the most defining feature of this genus is the large, pachyostic ribs and gastralia described as 'sausage-like' in profile.

facts.statement: Its barrel-shaped torso, short neck, and small flippers suggest it was not an agile swimmer.
facts.quote: This robust, barrel shaped torso, coupled with a relatively short neck and small flippers, indicate that it was not an agile swimmer.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen had five pairs of stout, conical teeth at the front of its lower jaw.
facts.quote: The holotypic specimen possessed five stout and conical tooth pairs on the mandibular symphysis

facts.statement: The head of Pachycostasaurus was about 20% of its total body length.
facts.quote: Its head was about 20% of overall body length, typical for most Pliosaurids of its time.

facts.statement: The specimen had at least 13 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: The specimen had a cervical vertebral count of at least 13

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Pachycostasaurus dawni measures approximately 3.1 meters in length.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, P. dawni, está representada por un solo espécimen casi completo (PETMG R338) que tenía aproximadamente 3,1 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The holotype possessed five pairs of thick, conical teeth on the mandibular symphysis.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotípico poseía cinco pares de dientes gruesos y cónicos en la sínfisis mandibular

facts.statement: Based on its anatomy, Pachycostasaurus was likely a benthic predator.
facts.quote: Judging by its anatomy, Pachycostasaurus was most probably a benthic predator.

facts.statement: Its teeth suggest a diet of soft teuthoids like belemnites, bony fish, and possibly larger reptiles.
facts.quote: The relative size and shape of its teeth indicate a diet ranging from soft teuthoids, such as belemnites, to bony fish, and perhaps some of the larger reptiles.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pachycostasaurus was allochthonous, having drifted into the marine basin from a freshwater or estuarine habitat.
facts.quote: The rarity of the animal in the formation may suggest that Pachycostasaurus was allochthonous.

facts.statement: Cruickshank suggested that Pachycostasaurus might have been allochthonous, living in coastal, freshwater, or deep-sea environments.
facts.quote: Cruickshank, sugirió que la rareza del animal en la formación puede sugerir que Pachycostasaurus fuera alóctono, su hábitat normal habría sido un entorno costero o incluso de agua dulce, o por otro lado un entorno de aguas profundas.

facts.statement: Pachycostasaurus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the Callovian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Pachycostasaurus belongs to the family Pliosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Pliosauridae

facts.statement: Its robust barrel-shaped torso, short neck, and small flippers indicate it was not an agile swimmer.
facts.quote: Tenía un torso robusto en forma de barril, un cuello relativamente corto y aletas pequeñas, lo que indica que no era un nadador ágil.

facts.statement: The cervical ribs were shortened, thickened, and double-headed.
facts.quote: Las costillas cervicales eran acortadas y engrosadas, así como de doble cabeza.

facts.statement: Pachycostasaurus likely played an important role in its food chain by transferring resources from the benthic to the surface food web.
facts.quote: Pachycostasaurus probablemente fue importante en su cadena alimentaria, ya que habría transferido recursos de la red alimentaria bentónica a la red alimentaria de la superficie a medida que surgía para respirar.

rejected.statement: Researchers doubt that Pachycostasaurus was a twist feeder like other contemporary pliosaurids.
rejected.quote: Thus it is doubtful if Pachycostasaurus was a twist feeder like other contemporary pliosaurids.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Pachycostasaurus was a twist feeder like other contemporary'
